questions.q: SELECT Name, (SELECT FirstName FROM Contacts) FROM Account returns what shape of result?
options: Only Accounts that have zero related Contacts
One row per Contact, with the related Account's Name flattened onto it
A flat list combining Account and Contact fields on the same row
One row per Account, each carrying a nested list of its related Contact records
questions.explain: Parent-to-child queries return the parent with a nested sub-list of children, the opposite shape of a child-to-parent dot-notation query.

questions.q: For a standard parent-to-child subquery on Account's related Contacts, what goes in the subquery's FROM clause?
options: Contact (the singular object name)
Contacts (the plural child object name)
Account.Contacts
Contact__r
questions.explain: For standard objects, the child relationship name used in a parent-to-child subquery is the plural name of the child object.

questions.q: If an Account has zero Contacts matching the subquery's WHERE clause, what happens?
options: The query throws a runtime error
The Account is excluded from the overall results entirely
The Account still comes back, with an empty nested list rather than being excluded
Salesforce substitutes a placeholder Contact record
questions.explain: A parent row isn't dropped just because its nested child subquery returns zero rows — it comes back with an empty nested list.

questions.q: For a custom child object accessed via a lookup field, what determines the relationship name used in a parent-to-child subquery?
options: The Child Relationship Name set on the lookup/master-detail field, editable in Setup at creation time
The child object's API name with no changes
Always exactly the plural of the object's label, with no way to change it
The name of the parent object, not the child
questions.explain: The child relationship name is a configurable property of the lookup/master-detail field, auto-generated as a plural __r name but editable in Setup.

questions.q: As of API version 58.0, how many levels of parent-to-child relationships can a single SOQL query nest?
options: There is no documented limit
Only one level
Up to ten levels
Up to five levels
questions.explain: Salesforce documents support for up to five levels of parent-to-child relationship nesting as of API version 58.0 and later.
